label: What Compy found

door.sub: Compy looks at what changed and tells you what it finds.
door.failed: Compy couldn't read its records just now. Nothing on your PC was changed.

problem.title: {{game}} has been running much rougher than usual
problem.body_one: In a normal session, {{game}}'s dips stay at about {{beforePct}}% of its average frame rate. In your last session they fell to about {{nowPct}}%.
problem.body_other: In a normal session, {{game}}'s dips stay at about {{beforePct}}% of its average frame rate. In your last {{count}} sessions they fell to about {{nowPct}}%.
problem.spikes: The slowest 1 in 100 frames took about {{nowMs}} ms, against about {{beforeMs}} ms in your normal sessions.
problem.average: It also averaged {{nowFps}} frames per second, against about {{beforeFps}} before.
problem.otherGames: {{games}} also had rough sessions in the same period.
problem.partial_one: Compy also saw 1 more session it only measured part of, and what it measured looked rough. A partly measured session never counts on its own.
problem.partial_other: Compy also saw {{count}} more sessions it only measured part of, and what it measured looked rough. A partly measured session never counts on its own.
problem.sinceLasted_one: It last ran normally on {{date}}. The rough run has lasted {{count}} session so far.
problem.sinceLasted_other: It last ran normally on {{date}}. The rough run has lasted {{count}} sessions so far.
problem.earlier: It also ran rough {{from}}–{{to}} and recovered.

answer.mechanism: Often causes this (not measured on your PC)

backgroundLoad.what: Other programs started while you played

memoryPressure.what: Your memory was nearly full while you played

settingDrift.applied: A setting Compy applied is no longer on

compyChange.what: Compy had a different number of changes on

displayRefreshLower.what: Your screen ran at a lower refresh rate

programInstalled.what: A program installed on {{day}} also started while you played

otherDriver.what: A driver other than graphics was updated

evidence.driverChanged: Your graphics driver changed from {{from}} to {{to}}.
evidence.sessionsSplit_one: {{game}}'s last normal session ({{date}}) used the old driver; the rough one used the new one.
evidence.sessionsSplit_other: {{game}}'s last normal session ({{date}}) used the old driver; all {{count}} rough ones used the new one.
evidence.crossGame: {{games}} also got much rougher after the update, and never before it.
evidence.installTimeNotRead: Compy didn't read the exact install time; it saw the new version on {{when}}.
evidence.roughOnOldDriver: {{count}} of the rough sessions were still on the old driver.
evidence.startsSeen: {{count}} of your rough sessions had other programs starting during them ({{names}}).
evidence.startsSeenNoNames: {{count}} of your rough sessions had other programs starting during them.
evidence.loadMeasured: Everything except the game used a lot of your processor in {{count}} of the rough sessions.
evidence.loadNotRecorded: Compy can't see programs that were already running, and didn't record how busy your PC was in these sessions.
evidence.ramPeak: Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB in one rough session.
evidence.ramBaseline: Your normal sessions peaked at {{peakGb}} GB.
evidence.ramWarning: Compy saw memory nearly full during that session.
evidence.ramLower: Other rough sessions only reached {{peakGb}} GB.
evidence.driftApplied: Compy's own check found a setting it applied is no longer on.
evidence.driftPower: Compy noticed the power plan was no longer performance-oriented.
evidence.driftOther: Compy noticed a setting it watches had changed.
evidence.whichNotRecorded: Which setting it was, and what changed it, isn't recorded.
evidence.countChanged: Compy had {{from}} changes on in the last normal session and {{to}} in the first rough one.
evidence.hardwareChanged: The graphics card or memory Compy recorded is different.
evidence.powerPlanChanged: The power plan recorded on the two sessions is different.
evidence.loadQuiet: Everything except the game was quiet in {{count}} of the rough sessions.
evidence.normalOnNewDriver_one: {{count}} session ran normally on the new driver (on {{date}}).
evidence.normalOnNewDriver_other: {{count}} sessions ran normally on the new driver (the latest on {{date}}).
evidence.partialRoughOnOldDriver: A partly measured session on {{date}}, on the old driver, also looked rough.
evidence.crossGameConfounded: {{games}}'s rough sessions had other programs starting during them, or have no load numbers, so this can't point to the driver alone.
evidence.capChanged: The frame cap went from {{from}} to {{to}}.
evidence.installRecorded: Windows recorded the driver install on {{when}}.
evidence.installNotRecorded: Windows has no record of a graphics driver install in this period, though the driver version Compy saw changed (it saw the new version on {{when}}).
evidence.installAfterRough: Windows recorded a graphics driver install on {{when}}, after the first rough session had started.
evidence.crossGameAfter: {{games}}'s rough sessions also came after the update.
evidence.updateMore_one: {{count}} more update was installed in the same period.
evidence.updateMore_other: {{count}} more updates were installed in the same period.
evidence.filesChanged: Steam says {{game}}'s files changed on {{when}}. That can be an update, a file verification or added content.
evidence.installedAndStarted: {{name}} was installed on {{day}} and also started during the rough sessions.
evidence.otherDriverInstalled_one: Windows recorded {{count}} {{classes}} driver install on {{when}}, and nothing else Compy found lines up with the timing.
evidence.otherDriverInstalled_other: Windows recorded {{count}} {{classes}} driver installs, the first on {{when}}, and nothing else Compy found lines up with the timing.
evidence.reinstallSameVersion: Windows recorded the same driver version being installed again on {{when}}.
evidence.installPriorUnknown: Windows recorded a graphics driver install on {{when}}; the version before it isn't known.
evidence.recoveredSameDriver: {{game}} ran normally again on the same driver ({{version}}), so the driver alone doesn't explain it.
evidence.recoveredAfterDriverChange: It recovered after the driver changed to {{version}} on {{when}}.
evidence.recoveredAfterDriverChangeSeen: It recovered after the driver changed to {{version}} (Compy first saw it on {{when}}).
evidence.recoveredQuiet: Compy saw no build or encoding program start, and the rest of your PC was quiet ({{pct}}% CPU used by other programs) in the session that ran normally.
evidence.roughLoadNotRecorded: Compy didn't record how busy the PC was in the rough sessions, so this comparison is one-sided.
evidence.recoveredBusy: Build or encoding programs were still starting, or the rest of your PC was busy, in a session that ran normally, so background programs alone don't explain it.
evidence.recoveredFewStarts: A few build or encoding programs started in the session that ran normally ({{starts}}), so Compy can't say the PC was quiet.
evidence.recoveryLoadNotRecorded: Compy didn't record how busy the PC was in the session that ran normally.
evidence.recoveredRamLower: Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB when it ran normally, against {{roughGb}} GB in the rough sessions.
evidence.recoveredRamFull: Memory still peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB when it ran normally, so memory alone doesn't explain it.
evidence.recoveryRamNotRead: Compy has no memory reading for the session that ran normally.
evidence.recoveredDriftStill: Compy's notice about that setting was already there before the session that ran normally, and it still stands, so that setting alone doesn't explain it.
evidence.recoveryDriftUnknown: Compy can't tell whether that setting was still off when it ran normally.
evidence.recoveredCompySame: Compy had {{count}} changes on when it ran normally, the same as in the rough sessions.
evidence.recoveredCompyBack: Compy's changes went from {{from}} to {{to}}, back to what they were in the normal sessions, before it ran normally.
evidence.recoveredCompyOther: Compy's changes went from {{from}} to {{to}} between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally.
evidence.recoveryCompyUnread: Compy has no change count for one of those sessions.
evidence.recoveredBuildSame: Windows was still build {{build}} when it ran normally, so that update alone doesn't explain it.
evidence.recoveredBuildChanged: Windows changed from build {{from}} to {{to}} between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally.
evidence.recoveryBuildUnread: Compy has no Windows build for one of those sessions.
evidence.recoveredUnchangedUpdate: Windows recorded no further update between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally, so the update was most likely still in place. It can't be the whole story on its own.
evidence.recoveredUnchangedFiles: Steam recorded no further change to {{game}}'s files between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally, so the files were most likely the same. They can't be the whole story on their own.
evidence.recoveredUnchangedProgram: Windows recorded no further program install between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally, so the program was most likely still there. It can't be the whole story on its own.
evidence.recoveredChangedAgainUpdate: Windows recorded another update on {{when}}, between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally.
evidence.recoveredChangedAgainFiles: Steam recorded another change to {{game}}'s files on {{when}}, between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally.
evidence.recoveredChangedAgainProgram: Windows recorded another program install on {{when}}, between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally.
evidence.recoveryRecordsUnread: Compy couldn't read Windows' records for the time since, so it can't say whether this changed again.
evidence.recoveredDriverRecordDiffers: Windows recorded a graphics driver install on {{when}} that the sessions' driver version doesn't show, so Compy can't say.
evidence.recoveryDriverUnread: Compy has no driver version for one of those sessions.
evidence.compyChangesDiffer: Compy's count of changes that are on also changed, from {{from}} to {{to}}, between the rough sessions and the one that ran normally.

fix.title: How to fix it

gpuDriver.step1: Press Windows + X and open Device Manager.
gpuDriver.step2: Open Display adapters, double-click your graphics card, then open the Driver tab.
gpuDriver.step3: If "Roll Back Driver" can be clicked, click it and restart. Your previous version was {{from}}.
gpuDriver.step4: If it's greyed out, download {{from}} from the graphics maker's previous-drivers page, run it, and choose the clean install option.
gpuDriver.step5: Then play {{game}} once and press Something's wrong again. Compy will compare it with how it usually runs.

backgroundLoad.step1NoNames: Close build tools, video encoders and download managers while you play.
backgroundLoad.step2: Play {{game}} once with them closed, then press Something's wrong again.

memoryPressure.step1: Close browser tabs and launchers before you play. Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB.
memoryPressure.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

settingDrift.step1: Open History to see what Compy changed, and check any Windows setting you changed yourself.
settingDrift.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

compyChange.step1: Open History and look at the changes Compy has on. Undo the newest one.
compyChange.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

fix.none: There's nothing safe Compy can change for this. Check it in Windows, then play once more.

frameCapChange.step1: Set the frame cap in the game or in your graphics settings back to what it was ({{from}}), or leave it as it is.
frameCapChange.step2: Play {{game}} a few times. Compy only compares like with like, and needs 3 normal sessions with the new setting.

windowsUpdate.step1: Open Settings, then Windows Update, then Update history to see what was installed and when.
windowsUpdate.stepUninstall: If you want to test it, Update history has "Uninstall updates". You can remove {{kb}} there and restart. That's your choice; Compy won't do it for you.
windowsUpdate.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

gameFiles.step1: Check {{game}}'s patch notes for what changed around that date.
gameFiles.step2: In Steam, right-click {{game}}, open Properties, then Installed Files, and choose Verify integrity of game files.
gameFiles.step3: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

programInstalled.step1: Close {{names}} while you play, or uninstall it if you don't need it.
programInstalled.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

card.notProven: Compy can't prove this until you try the fix and play again.
card.scrollLabel: What Compy found. Scrolls if there is more.

why.crossGame: It changed just before {{game}} got rough, and {{games}} got rough right after it too. The other changes don't line up with every rough session.
why.tie: Two changes line up equally. Start with the one that's easier to undo.
why.crossGameLead: It changed just before {{game}} got rough, and {{games}} got rough right after it too.

checked.memoryPressure: Memory: never reached {{percent}}% full in these sessions.

checked.gameFiles: Steam hasn't recorded an update to {{game}} since {{when}}.
checked.gpuDriverNoInstall: Graphics driver: still {{driver}}. Windows recorded no graphics driver install in this period.

unknown.overlays: Which overlays or recorders were running
unknown.otherLoad: How busy the rest of your PC was while you played
unknown.gpuDriver: Which graphics driver was in use

nothingWrong.title: Nothing looks wrong
nothingWrong.body_one: {{game}}'s last session ran the way it usually does. If something still feels off, tell Compy what you notice and play once more with Compy running.
nothingWrong.body_other: {{game}}'s last {{count}} sessions ran the way it usually does. If something still feels off, tell Compy what you notice and play once more with Compy running.

cantTell.title: Compy can't tell yet
cantTell.needsMore: Compy needs {{total}} normal sessions of {{game}} to know what normal is. You have {{have}}.
cantTell.partial: Compy only measured part of your last {{game}} session ({{percent}}%), so it won't judge it. Play once more with Compy running.
cantTell.noGame: Compy hasn't recorded {{game}} yet. Start Compy before you play.
cantTell.noSessions: Compy hasn't recorded any games yet. Start Compy before you play.
cantTell.crash: Crashes have their own page for now. Open Problems to see what Windows recorded.
cantTell.partialRough: Compy only measured part of your last {{game}} session ({{percent}}%), and what it saw looked rough. Play once more with Compy running.
cantTell.frameCap: Your frame cap changed, or Compy can't read it, between your earlier {{game}} sessions and the newest one, so it won't compare them.
cantTell.backToNormal: Compy can't tell yet whether {{game}} is back to normal. Play once more.

nothingChanged.title: Compy measured the problem, but nothing it records changed before it
nothingChanged.next: Play once more and Compy will compare again.

footer: Compy lists what changed before the problem. It doesn't claim to know the cause until a fix is checked.

notSeparable.title: Compy can't tell which of these it is yet
notSeparable.next: To find out: play {{game}} once with nothing else running. Compy will compare.
notSeparable.nextOther: Play {{game}} once more. Compy may still not be able to tell these apart.

seen.updatesMinor: {{n}} security definition and {{m}} app updates (listed for completeness).
seen.programsInstalledMore: {{count}} programs were installed on {{day}}: {{names}} and {{more}} more.
seen.programsNone: No program with a recorded install date was installed in this period.
seen.otherDrivers_one: {{count}} other driver was installed in this period ({{classes}}).
seen.otherDrivers_other: {{count}} other drivers were installed in this period ({{classes}}).
seen.driverInstallSameStamp: Windows recorded a graphics driver install on {{when}}, but the driver version on your sessions didn't change.
seen.driverOtherInstall: Windows recorded a graphics driver install on {{when}} for a different version than the one your rough sessions ran on.

limit.notSteam: Compy couldn't match {{game}} to a Steam install, so it can't see when it was updated.
limit.classes: Compy reads graphics, audio, network and chipset driver installs only, not other drivers.
limit.noInstallDate: Compy can't see Store apps, or programs that don't record an install date ({{n}} here).

why.accessDenied: Windows needs administrator rights to show that log
why.logEmpty: that Windows log is empty or switched off
why.logMissing: this PC has no such Windows log
why.recordsUnreadable: Windows returned {{n}} records Compy couldn't read
why.registry: the list of installed programs couldn't be opened
why.steamNoRecord: Steam has no record of this game
why.steamNoTime: Steam's record has no update time
why.notRead: Compy didn't look it up for this answer
why.tookTooLong: reading took too long, so Compy went on without it
why.noWindow: there was no period to look at
why.partialTimedOut: reading ran out of time, so only the newest records were read
why.partialRowCap: the log holds more records than Compy reads, so older ones are missing
why.partialOutputCapped: the log was too long to read in full
why.partialSteamLibraries: {{n}} Steam library folders couldn't be read
why.partialCoverage: Windows' log only goes back to {{from}}

verdict.likely: One change lines up best with what happened. It's listed first.
verdict.possible: A change lines up with when it started, but Compy can't prove it.

next.likely: Try the steps under the first one, play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.
next.possible: Check it, play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again. Compy will compare.

recovered.title: {{game}} is running the way it usually does again
recovered.numbers: Its dips stayed at about {{beforePct}}% of its average before, fell to about {{roughPct}}% while it was rough, and are at about {{nowPct}}% now.
recovered.basisOne: Its newest session ran at or above its usual.
recovered.basisTwo: Its last two sessions both ran close to its usual.
recovered.nothing: Compy can't narrow it down from this recovery.
recovered.next: If it runs rough again, press Something's wrong again and Compy will compare.
recovered.notProven: This is what the recorded sessions show. It doesn't prove why it got better.
